title: Brazil x Argentina: classic decides Olympic spot
seoTitle: Brazil vs Argentina: Classic Decides Olympic Spot
subtitle: The clash at Maracanãzinho could secure early qualification for the Los Angeles Olympic Games
excerpt: The classic between Brazil and Argentina in the South American volleyball championship, held this Sunday at Maracanãzinho, could decide the early Olympic spot.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: ge, LANCE!, Clube de Regatas do Flamengo
contentHtml:
The classic between Brazil and Argentina, scheduled for this Sunday at 10 AM at the Maracanãzinho Gymnasium, could decide who secures early qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games. The match brings together two undefeated teams and promises an intense confrontation.

Beating Argentina, Brazil Secures Olympic Spot

Brazil enters the final match of the South American Championship with a 100% record, having beaten Chile, Bolivia, Colombia, and Venezuela by 3 sets to 0. Argentina also arrives undefeated, with 3-0 victories over the same opponents. The clash at Maracanãzinho pits the two strongest campaigns of the competition against each other, determining the South American champion, as well as the team that will claim the coveted Olympic spot.

Matheus Pinta Faces Horacio Dileo in a Duel of Leaders

Middle blocker Matheus Pinta, who plays for both the national team and Campinas, will compete in the classic against Argentina, where Argentine coach Horacio Dileo, who is also Pinta's club coach, will lead the 'Albiceleste' team. Pinta, who previously played against Dileo in the Copa Brasil, commented that the Argentine “knows his style well” and that he intends to surprise him.

Performance of Coaches Bernardinho and Dileo

Bernardinho, coach of the Brazilian national team, has also held the position at Sesc-Flamengo and boasts experience across 10 Superliga seasons. Dileo, meanwhile, will complete 10 seasons at the helm of his Brazilian club in the upcoming Superliga. Both are described as “very combative” and “tough,” but Pinta notes that Bernardinho “scolds more.”

Brazil's Path in the South American Championship

Brazil defeated Venezuela by 3 sets to 0, with Matheus Pinta being the third-highest scorer on the team, recording seven points in the match. The national team maintains the tournament lead and has already secured the South American title, with five wins in five matches and 15 sets won, without dropping a single set.

Impact on the Olympic Scenario

The classic between Brazil and Argentina not only decides the continental title but also the early qualification spot for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games. The winning team will stamp its Olympic passport and secure its presence in the next edition of the Games.
